analysis.title: Asset Management Market Flash: The Fed changes gear
key_insights: October US CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 0.3% ex food and energy, above the 0.3% analysts expected, and markets took a December Fed rate hike as given.

FOMC member Christopher Waller warned this inflation level would warrant a 50bp hike in December. The report says a half-point hike is still unlikely, since it might be seen as excessive and no other Fed official, including Beth Hammack, has backed it.

The US 10-year yield moved back above 5% and the 2-year rose more, pricing about 85bp of additional tightening by end 2027. Gold fell below $4,000/oz and the euro fell below 1.105 against a stronger dollar.
The Fed's shift in tone is attributed to persistent inflationary pressure from AI investment and energy prices.

Geopolitical hopes for detente faded: Iran still refuses to release enriched uranium, Trump says he does not need an agreement, and Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi produced only a prisoner exchange. Brent fell to a 10-week low, then rebounded toward $96 on Thursday.
Oil's earlier decline rested on peace hopes, Gulf crude exports at pre-war levels and sharply lower maritime freight rates. The report says these improvements depend on no fresh military escalation.

Nvidia fell 11% after founder Jensen Huang resigned over revelations about his personal life, and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. The report says uncertainty centers on the successor and legal risk rather than the business, and the tech sector was not dragged down.
US equities rebounded: S&P 500 +2.9%, Nasdaq 100 +4.8%, Russell 2000 +1.7%, tech +3.8%, SOX +12%. WTI fell 2% to $89.

CoreWeave rose 22% after sales beat consensus by 3%. Cisco rose 9% on adjusted EPS 6% above expectations and a full-year EPS outlook 8% above consensus, with AI infrastructure revenue now expected to reach $9bn.

Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow: 825 million shares at $70-78, up to $64bn, valuing the company at $1.25-1.4 trillion diluted. Pricing is set for November 18 and Nasdaq trading starts the day after.
Healthcare underperformed: Moderna fell 9% after giving no 2027 forecast, and Ionis fell 31% after cutting 2026 Tryngolza sales guidance from $100m to $50m on a slower rollout.

Utilities gained 2%: Constellation Energy rose 13% on adjusted EPS 31% above consensus, and Vistra rose 8% on adjusted EBITDA 11% above expectations, a higher full-year guide and $1.5bn of additional buybacks.

European indices hit new highs on lower oil prices and solid earnings. Investors expect an ECB hike in December, and eurozone finance ministers began discussing a successor to Lagarde. Industrials tied to data centres and power grids led, with Siemens Energy jumping on record results.
ASML and other European semiconductor names continued to suffer from AI doubts, while Infineon reassured on data centre power demand.
Emerging markets: MSCI EM rose 3.5% in USD, with Taiwan and Korea each recovering over 9%. India rose 1.4%, China fell 2.9% on concerns over AI computing access, and Brazil fell 0.9%.
China October CPI was 0.7% y/y (0.9% in September) and PPI 5.7% y/y. Exports grew 35.2% y/y and imports 41.6%. Authorities are reportedly considering a 25% income tax on government bond interest.

Taiwan activated its National Stabilisation Fund and tightened short-selling limits. TSMC October revenue rose 15% m/m and 60% y/y. Korea's semiconductor exports rose 33.1% y/y to $16.6bn in November 1-10, nearly half of total exports.
The rupiah hit a record low and the central bank intervened, after Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned. Peru raised its rate 25bp to 4.50%, its first hike in nearly four years.

Credit: the 10-year Treasury yield rose 27bp on the week to 5.12% and the 2-year rose 37bp. European high yield returned 0.60% and the CoCo index 0.35%, with the Xover tighter by 20bp. Investment grade fell 0.14% on higher yields.
The firm's stance: the AI theme should keep supporting global equities, with valuations back at attractive levels, while it diversifies into other regions and bonds for decorrelation.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell 11% after founder Jensen Huang resigned, with Colette Kress interim CEO. The report puts the uncertainty on his successor and legal risk, not the business.

sector_views.rationale: The AI theme is expected to keep underpinning global equities, and valuations are described as back at attractive levels.
The firm is diversifying into bonds, which it says now offer the advantage of decorrelation.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave: sales beat consensus by 3% (reported, week of 11/13), shares +22%.
Cisco: adjusted EPS beat consensus by 6% (reported), full-year EPS outlook 8% above consensus, AI infrastructure revenue now expected to reach $9bn, shares +9%.
Constellation Energy: adjusted EPS 31% above consensus (reported), annual EPS guidance 5% above expectations, shares +13%.
Vistra: adjusted EBITDA 11% above expectations (reported) on Texas, full-year guidance raised, additional $1.5bn buybacks, shares +8%.
Moderna: investor day confirmed 2026 sales growth of 15% to 25% but gave no 2027 forecast, shares -9%.
Ionis Pharmaceuticals: cut 2026 Tryngolza sales forecast from $100m to $50m on a slower rollout, shares -31%.

Europe: Burberry sales beat expectations, Richemont margins hurt by higher gold prices, Siemens Energy reported record results with a big dividend increase, Siemens raised medium-term guidance, Merck KGaA raised guidance, Brenntag quarterly figures missed expectations, Generali beat expectations.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above the 0.3% analysts expected, and it led markets to price a December Fed hike.

macro_indicators.indicator: US core CPI m/m (ex food and energy)

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up 27bp on the week, back above 5%.
Prices about 85bp of additional tightening by end 2027.
Rebounded from a 10-week low on renewed Middle East tensions.
Down from 0.9% in September on food prices.
Driven by higher energy and chemical prices.
Waller said this level of inflation would warrant it. The report calls the odds slight.

risk_factors: A 50bp Fed hike in December would be seen as excessive and could trigger market turbulence.
Renewed military escalation in the Middle East would reverse the recent oil and freight improvement.
Nvidia's leadership succession and legal risk, and possible tighter US chip restrictions on China.
Inflation pressure from AI investment and energy prices.
Rupiah weakness and political uncertainty in Indonesia.
vol_and_positioning: Bond volatility remained high, especially in the US, after hawkish Fed comments.
Taiwan tightened short-selling restrictions and activated its National Stabilisation Fund after the sharp correction.
geopolitical: Iran still refuses to release its enriched uranium and Trump says he does not need an agreement.
Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi produced only a prisoner exchange.
Israel's ambassador to the UN said Washington sent troops to the Middle East to prepare for another attack on Iran.
Gulf crude exports are running at pre-war levels and maritime freight rates have fallen, conditional on no fresh military escalation.
Concern grew over tighter US restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips following the Jensen Huang controversy.
The US Department of Defence removed WuXi AppTec from its Chinese Military Companies List after a court ruling.

tension_points.bull_case: A 50bp hike is unlikely: it might be seen as excessive, and no other Fed official, not even Beth Hammack, has backed Waller's idea.
tension_points.bear_case: Waller said this inflation level would warrant 50bp. Markets already take a December hike as given and 2-year yields price about 85bp more tightening by end 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Other Fed officials backing Waller's call for a 50bp December hike.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent fell to a 10-week low on peace hopes, Gulf crude exports are at pre-war levels and freight rates have tumbled.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran refuses to release enriched uranium, Trump says he does not need a deal, and Israel's UN ambassador said US troops were sent to prepare another attack on Iran.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fresh military escalation, on which the improvement in exports and freight is conditional.
